sources: dossier=Net position line 10: 'rimsky_lineage is an append-only projection with two record kinds: leaf_run ... and claim_terminal (renamed from claim_commit; outcome discriminator committed | abandoned | force_cancelled)'; Required behaviors line 20: 'claim_terminal records carry version_id and the outcome discriminator (committed/abandoned/force_cancelled) making claim resolutions queryable from lineage'; doc=lineage.md:22 (pre-edit) said the projection writer runs 'at claim-handle commit', contradicting the doc's own line 13 ('captures every claim-handle terminal') and concept:lineage-record invariant 3; code=terminal_decision_forensics.go::terminalOutcomeKey/emitTerminalForensics writes WriteClaimTerminalLineage for commit, abandon, and force-cancel alike
note: Dossier's three-valued outcome discriminator only makes sense if claim-terminal records are written at every terminal disposition, not only commit; doc line 22 was an isolated stale phrase contradicting the rest of the same doc. Corrected to 'claim-handle terminal (commit, natural abandon, or force-cancelled abandon)'.

sources: dossier=Intentional absences: 'Retention coupling (delete lineage rows whose artifacts were swept): never implemented; retention is flat trailing-window and always was. Adjudicated fix-doc, finding 448 (2026-07-13, transcript). This supersedes the 2026-05-15 plan language describing artifact-coupled deletion.'; Net position line 4: 'Lineage retention is a flat trailing window (default 30d) and has been since day one'; doc=lineage.md:32 (pre-edit) said retention lasts 'as long as the corresponding artifact ... is retained, plus a configurable trailing window'; code=retention_sweeps.go::SweepLineageRetention computes cutoff=now.Add(-cfg.LineageTrailing) with no reference to run/claim retention
note: Dossier explicitly rules this fix-doc at transcript tier, naming finding 448 by id. Retention section rewritten to describe the flat, artifact-independent trailing window.

sources: dossier=Intentional absences: 'Lineage rebuild-from-events as a present capability: always "deferred V1" intent; a corpus-bootstrap edit stripped the qualifier and wrongly converted it to a present-tense ownership claim. Adjudicated fix-doc, finding 449 (2026-07-13, 3f71f90a, transcript).'; Superseded/historical line 53 confirms the same; doc=lineage.md:17 (pre-edit) 'Owns: ... the projection-rebuild path' and :11/:22 'rebuildable from ...'; code=only forward writers exist (lineage_writer.go, terminal_decision_forensics.go), no rebuild/reconstruct code found by grep
note: Dossier explicitly rules this fix-doc at transcript tier, naming finding 449 by id. Removed 'the projection-rebuild path' from Boundaries Owns, and reworded Definition/Invariants to say the projection is written forward from the audit log and claim-handle lifecycle rather than rebuildable/reconstructable from them.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 19 only says 'forward/reverse walks over control-api, depth-bounded (max 50)' and 'query by claim handle' as a point lookup, without specifying whether claim-handle walks are meant to be bidirectional like run walks (2026-05-15 + 2026-06-08, artifact); doc=lineage.md:28 (unedited) claims 'recursive backward/forward walks across runs and claim handles'; code=controlapi/lineage.go registers runs/{id}/ancestors+descendants but only claims/{id}/ancestors (which per the finding's correction actually walks sub_claim_handle_ids, i.e. children/descendants, so the one existing claim route is itself mislabeled)
note: Design-call: the dossier never specifies whether claim-handle lineage walks were meant to be symmetric (ancestors+descendants) like run walks, or one-directional by design (e.g. only the claim-tree descendant walk matters for lineage). Question for a human: should a claims/{id}/descendants (or renamed/corrected) route be added to match the doc, or should the doc be narrowed to the one direction that exists — and separately, should the existing 'ancestors' route be renamed since it functionally walks children? Left lineage.md:28 unedited pending this decision.

sources: dossier=silent on the specific runtime-vs-static mechanism for substitution refs (Required behaviors line 20 only says leaf_run records 'carry substitution refs' without specifying capture timing); corroborated by concept:node-subscription invariants: 'Every substitution ref in a node's attribute schema is matched at registration against the receiver's subscription declarations' — refs are a statically-declared, registration-time construct, not a runtime-observed lookup log; doc=lineage.md:11 (pre-edit) said 'every {{nodes.X.attribute.Y}} lookup the executor's attribute template performed'; code=lineage_writer.go::CollectSubstitutionRefsForEmit calls graphnode.SubstitutionRefsFromAttributes (static extraction from the node def) then mostRecentRunIDForNode to bind each sender to its latest leaf-run
note: concept:node-subscription (design corpus, independent of code) already establishes substitution refs as statically declared per the node's attribute schema and validated at registration, which corroborates the code's static-extraction mechanism and contradicts the doc's 'lookup ... performed' runtime-capture phrasing. Reworded to 'reference declared in the node's attribute schema ... citation to the sender's most recent run'.
